presentation:
A 66-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes on metformin 1000 mg BID and oral semaglutide (Rybelsus 3 mg) presents with persistent hyperglycemia and unintended weight loss. She has a past medical history of carpal tunnel release surgery 8 years ago. She discontinued pioglitazone and sitagliptin due to osteoporosis. Despite no GI side effects on Rybelsus, she has lost 5 lbs (now 104 lbs) since starting it one month ago. She reports fasting and post-prandial glucose readings as follows:

Fasting glucose >200 mg/dL
Post-prandial glucose 150–200 mg/dL

Her A1c and weight over the past year:

12 months ago: A1c 7.4%, 109 lbs
6 months ago: A1c 7.5%, 108 lbs
1 month ago: A1c 8.1%, 109 lbs
Today: 104 lbs

BMI is 19.7 today Patient is willing to switch to an injectable GLP-1 receptor agonist to improve blood sugar control while minimizing further weight loss. Would dulaglutide would be appropriate?
